event.summary: Shared lifecycle helper releases its holds on error
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: Investigated whether extracting lifecycle orchestration could leave a host permanently disconnected after Suspend or Resume. Source refutes a stranded-hold route in the assigned helper. Details: perform takes the initial hold for Suspend or disconnected Resume; a real Resume from a supposedly connected actor takes it after transition. transition and record errors are captured in result before the final release decision. hold_connection atomically publishes a non-connected state and sets hold (manager.rs:1604-1627), so a hold taken here always enters the final not-connected branch. release_hold clears hold and nudges the actor (1651-1661), including successful Podman Suspend whose record callback returns None (environment/podman.rs:682-719). The actor then rechecks status. Tensorlake validates key before perform (tensorlake/lifecycle.rs:81-100), keeps attribution recording within the error-capturing block, and repeated connected Running Resume takes no hold. Contract SPEC_impl.md Tensorlake hosts: 'Every failure releases the hold' and 'Only an already-running sandbox with an already-connected actor skips recovery, preserving its viewers on repeated Resume.' Suggested bucket: high if stranding had existed; could-be-highest: no, the considered issue was availability without established loss of work/security. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for this concern. proposed_drop: source refutation above. possible_cover: none. Source-only; no execution. Cancellation is excluded by existing owned request and automatic-start tasks, not by this helper itself.
